title: Elderly fall on Eliquis - evolving TBI
objectives: Treat 'lift assist' as a full assessment; anticoagulant + head strike = trauma center risk factor (4.9)
Spinal assessment per 4.6 algorithm; SMR when indicated
Serial GCS/pupils; recognize deterioration & Cushing's triad (HTN, bradycardia, irregular resp)
TBI bundle: SpO2 > 94, SBP >= 110, EtCO2 35-45, no hyperventilation
Manage family pressure to not transport
resources: Collar/SMR, scoop, O2/NRB, BVM w/ capno, IV, suction. UVMMC (Level 1, neurosurgery) ~7 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to 6 Elm Court for a lift assist. 82-year-old female fell, uninjured per caller. Caller is her son. Time out 1920.

scene.location: Kitchen floor, ranch home. Throw rug bunched near table.
scene.setup: Pt sitting on floor against cabinet, small bump on forehead, son trying to lift her by arms as you arrive.
scene.moulage: Purple bruise/egg R forehead, skin tear L forearm (gauze wrap).
scene.roles: Pt actor; son (wants a quick lift - "she's fine, she's done this before").

patient.name: Irene Tatro
patient.on_arrival: Alert, chatty, embarrassed, sitting on floor. Hematoma R forehead. Mild neck stiffness when turning.

SAMPLE: **Apixaban (Eliquis) 5 mg BID**, metoprolol 25 mg, levothyroxine 50 mcg
Afib, HTN, hypothyroid, prior hip replacement
Tripped on rug ~1845, hit head on table edge. Unsure if LOC. On floor ~30 min

primary: Forehead hematoma; check hips (prior replacement) - normal
Looks stable; **high-risk TBI** (age + anticoagulant + head strike)
secondary: 4 cm hematoma R forehead, no deformity
Skin tear L forearm; CSM intact x4

vitals.other: Afib on monitor. Repeats "did I fall?"
L-sided weakness. Cushing's triad (rising BP w/ widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, irregular respirations)
Point out on capno; correct to 10/min

vitals.trigger: Examiner inject, any time after T+8
vitals.other: SBP < 110 in TBI (GCS/pupils unchanged). After NS 1 L: BP 118/70. HR blunted by metoprolol

flow.give: Son lifting her by arms: "She's fine, just help me get her up."
Stage **A**. Neck tender at C5-6 if palpated. Show MED LIST card if asked about meds.
Pt: "I don't want to go, it's just a bump." Son agrees.

branches.then: Stage **B** begins in front of them; capacity now in question

branches.if: Son: "It's 7 min, I'll drive her myself" - crew agrees

expected: Transport decision: trauma center (4.9 risk factors)

flow.give: Stage **B** -> vomits. Then Stage **C** at T+15.
expected: O2 NRB; BVM if RR inadequate at 10/min

flow.give: Son asks to ride along. Check vent rate and SBP.

branches.if: BP drops to 100/60 (any time after T+8)
branches.then: Stage **F**; expect IV + NS 1 L (4.10), HOB flat if SBP < 100, search for 2nd bleed source

expected: Report: anticoagulant, GCS trend, pupils, last dose
SIREN: serial neuro exams w/ times

critical: No spinal assessment / SMR with midline tenderness
Refusal accepted without capacity assessment / with confusion
SBP < 110 not treated with fluid / not rechecked q3-5 min (4.10)
No suction ready after vomiting / airway not protected
POV transport allowed / no TRAUMA ALERT
differentials: Elderly, anticoagulated, head strike, delayed decline
Trauma history; treat as TBI, still time-critical
debrief: Which 4.9 risk factors applied even though vitals were normal?
Why are anticoagulated head injuries 'talk and deteriorate'?
Cushing's triad (rising BP w/ widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, irregular respirations) - what did you see and when?
Why does hyperventilation harm TBI patients?
How do you turn a 'lift assist' into an assessment without fighting the family?

crew_card.dispatch: 6 Elm Court. Lift assist. 82 y/o F fell, uninjured per caller. Caller: son.
crew_card.on_arrival: Kitchen. Elderly woman on floor against cabinet, bump on forehead. Son is pulling her up by the arms.

actor_card.Act: Pleasant, embarrassed, chatty. Ask "did I fall?" twice early on.
actor_card.Want: "I don't need the hospital, it's just a bump."
actor_card.~T+10: Say headache is worse, nauseated, vomit (fake), sleepy.
actor_card.~T+15: Slurred, only respond to loud voice, L arm/leg weak.
actor_card.Son: "She's fine, she's fallen before." Accepts transport if crew explains Eliquis risk.

learn_more.topic: traumatic brain injury in an older adult on apixaban after a ground-level fall
learn_more.focus: anticoagulated head injury risk, avoiding hypotension (SBP >= 110), hypoxia and hyperventilation, and Cushing's triad
